Globalist v. Nationalist

Globalist: A globalist believes that humanity is one big family. There should be no such thing as borders. Everyone worldwide should fall under one set of governance, regardless what that government is. You are a globalist if you agree with free and open borders, and if you are against national sovereignty.

Nationalist: A nationalist puts their country first. A nationalist can be empathetic to the struggles of other countries but would like to focus on internal problems first. If you believe that your countries homeless problem is more important than refugee resettlement, you are most likely a nationalist. If you believe in your countries sovereignty and would like to preserve your culture or way of thinking you fit this category.

Communist v. Socialist v. Capitalist

Communism: At it's base philosophy, communists believe the people will put into society according to their ability. The people will then take from society according to their needs. The government will own all property, including housing and businesses. the government will dictate how the goods of the nation are distributed. People will likely be told where to work to ensure a well oiled society.

Socialism: True socialism is not far from communism however there are some differences. Socialists also believe that people will put into society according to their ability. However, the people will take from society according to their contribution to it. Socialists believe the government should control all industry. There is little to no room for private business. However, the people can own their own property, as in land and homes.

Capitalism: Capitalists believe that government should have little to no influence over industry. A person who builds a business is entitled to keep all the proceeds that come with it. A person is as successful as what they make of themselves. Individual rights to property are of no business to the government. Also, the wages that a business owner offers are his own choice and shouldn't be regulated.

Examples:

If your country allows illegal immigrants to enter and immediately receive welfare, this would be a communist program, not socialist. The reason being is that the individual had not contributed anything to the host nation to be awarded the benefit. i.e. the person will be expected to contribute according to his ability and take according to his needs.

If a person works their entire life and pays into social security, to collect "retirement" at a determined age, this would be an example of a socialist program. The person has contributed a lifetime of work and is now taking according to his contributions. The Obama-phone is not a socialist program, as the people receiving the phone are not required to have contributed anything. Again, this is a communist policy.

Capitalists are individualists, and for the most part, want to be left alone. They don't really want any policies regulating how people make money.
